description: The plot shows how three accuracy-related measures vary with initial confidence, with three lines (Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy) plotted against the same x-axis. The x-axis is labeled “Initial Confidence,” uses a linear scale, and spans from 0.86 to 1.00 with tick labels shown at 0.86, 0.88, 0.89, 0.90, …, 1.00 (i.e., mostly 0.01 spacing, with 0.87 not shown). The y-axis is labeled “Accuracy,” uses a linear scale, and runs from 0.0 to 1.0 with labeled ticks every 0.2. The blue solid line with circular markers (Final Accuracy) starts near 0.93 at 0.86 and remains high across the range, reaching about 1.00 around 0.98–0.99 and ending just under 1.00 (about 0.98) at 1.00. The orange dashed line with diamond markers (Δ Accuracy) begins around 0.28 at 0.86, declines through the mid-range to its lowest values near 0.05 around 0.95, then rises again, ending around 0.20 at 1.00. The green dashed line with square markers (Initial Accuracy) starts around 0.64 at 0.86, increases overall to roughly 0.92–0.93 around 0.95–0.96, stays near ~0.88–0.92 through 0.99, and then drops to about 0.77 at 1.00. All three series include vertical error bars at each x-value.
caption_used: The line plot illustrates the relationship between Initial Confidence and different measures of Accuracy (Final Accuracy, ∆ Accuracy, Initial Accuracy). The x-axis represents 'Initial Confidence' on a linear scale, ranging from 0.86 to 1.00, with tick labels at intervals of 0.01 except that 0.87 is missing. The y-axis represents 'Accuracy,' also on a linear scale, ranging from 0.0 to 1.0, with tick labels at intervals of 0.2. The blue line, representing 'Final Accuracy,' uses circle markers and a solid line style. It starts at approximately 0.9 and steadily increases to reach 1.0 at the highest confidence level. The orange line, denoting '∆ Accuracy,' features diamond markers and a dashed line style, beginning near 0.3 at 0.86 and showing a sharp decline to below 0.05 at 0.95, before stabilizing at around 0.1. The green line, indicating 'Initial Accuracy,' uses square markers with a dashed line style. It starts at about 0.65, showing a gradual increase to around 0.95 before plateauing at the highest confidence level. All three lines include error bars, indicating variability at each data point. The Final Accuracy consistently exceeds Initial Accuracy across all confidence levels, as shown in the plot.
